recorded.rule: Q2 v2: a giveaway, read from the question's own text alone
recorded.prompt:q-reversed: Answer ONLY from this question's own text: its stem and its options. Use no knowledge of the subject at all; treat every term as a word you have never met. Pick an option only when the wording itself singles it out: it is longer or more specific than the others, it repeats words from the stem, the others carry absolute terms such as 'always' or 'never', the stem's grammar fits it alone, or it restates the stem. A cue decides only when it clearly singles out one option over every other; a weak cue, or one another option shares, decides nothing. Otherwise answer 'none'. Say which cue decided it, or that none did.
recorded.pass:q-reversed: an independent agent given Q2_PROMPT, the stem and the options, never the page
recorded.outcome:q-reversed: from the question's text alone, the reader picked none; the key is 'a'
recorded.because:q-reversed: All three options follow the same 'With ...' pattern and are about the same length. None repeats the stem more than the others or uses absolute terms.

recorded.prompt:q-reversed:b: Does a passage of the page rule this wrong option out?
recorded.pass:q-reversed:b: an independent agent given the page and the keyed question
recorded.outcome:q-reversed:b: the page rules this option out
recorded.because:q-reversed:b: Pitfall 5 gives the cause as 'the chained call gives the lambda no target type, so b is inferred as Object', and Comparator.comparing(Box::size).reversed() compiles even though it boxes the int key (comparingInt 'also avoids boxing'), so boxed keys can be reversed.
recorded.prompt:q-reversed:c: Does a passage of the page rule this wrong option out?
recorded.pass:q-reversed:c: an independent agent given the page and the keyed question
recorded.outcome:q-reversed:c: the page rules this option out
recorded.because:q-reversed:c: Pitfall 5 says 'A method reference carries its type, so the same chain compiles', a compile-time reason rather than a check deferred to run time.
recorded.prompt:q-negate:a: Does a passage of the page rule this wrong option out?
recorded.pass:q-negate:a: an independent agent given the page and the keyed question
recorded.outcome:q-negate:a: the page rules this option out
recorded.because:q-negate:a: Pitfall 2 says 'cannot write !String::isBlank as a method reference' and marks filter(!String::isBlank) as a compile error.
recorded.prompt:q-negate:c: Does a passage of the page rule this wrong option out?
recorded.pass:q-negate:c: an independent agent given the page and the keyed question
recorded.outcome:q-negate:c: the page rules this option out
recorded.because:q-negate:c: Q1's code comment says 'A method reference has no type of its own until assigned, so give it one before calling andThen', and Pitfall 3 needs a cast before chaining, so :: does not already give a Predicate to call .negate() on; the page's fix is Predicate.not.
